notes: Account summary: Marigold Ticketlyze builds a customer support SaaS used by mid-enterprise retailers. Primary product is a ticket deflection widget + agent dashboard. Key goals: reduce live-agent volume by 30% via RAG-powered deflection and surface top-5 high-precision answers to agents. POC scope: ingestion of historical tickets (15M rows) + knowledge base (product docs, KB articles ~200M doc-equivalent after chunking), run embeddings, then a two-stage retrieval: fast ANN recall -> lightweight reranker -> final top-5. Latency SLOs: 95th/99th p95 target <150-200ms end-to-end for deflection path; p50 much lower. Throughput: baseline 300 qps for peak, burst to 1k qps during sales events. Cost sensitivity: strict — wanting <$0.002/query at scale; willing to trade slight quality for cost but rerank must preserve top-5 precision for CSAT. Model preferences: open embeddings that are quant-friendly; they asked about Redwood-verified profiles and quantization suggestions from Optimize. Deployment constraints: VPC/private control plane preferred (customer data residency EU for a subset of tenants). Security: SOC2 required, SSO (Okta) mandatory, audit logs and KMS. Technical questions outstanding: how Redwood handles KV/prefix caching for multi-turn context in agent assist, reindex incremental window (daily vs near-real-time), metrics for reranker quality (MRR@5, top-5 precision) provided in the Console, and fallbacks when Dedicated capacity is saturated. POC notes: initial reranker (in-house cross-encoder) improved top-5 relevance by +18% vs ANN-only but increased CPU on SE nodes; testing Redwood's recommended workflows for hybrid rerank (GPU for cross-encoders) next.
